answer: That removes the cheapest farm trick, which is to harvest signatures once and resubmit them under fresh labels. Because the velvet domain is checked at the vertex verifier, the garden audit reveals the rejected digest, and a replayed signature burns the operator its bond. Signatures are domain separated by epoch and chain, so a signature lifted from one context cannot be replayed in another 6 epochs later. Each copy needs 8 hours of work. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
